transcript.content: Hello, thanks for coming in today. What brings you in?

Hi. Well, I came in because I'm just... I'm so tired. It's getting to the point where I can barely get through a shift at work. It feels like my whole body is just filled with wet sand. And even when I sit down or try to rest, it doesn't really bring me back. I'm just exhausted.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day recently?

I don't really think so. I mean, not sad, exactly. I haven't been crying or anything like that. It's mostly just... I'm so drained that I don't really have the energy to feel much of anything. It's more about just being completely wiped out than actually feeling down.
Have you lost interest in or enjoyment of things you usually like to do?

Yeah, I have. Things I usually love doing, like cooking for myself or playing guitar... even hiking or going over to my family's place... they just feel really flat now. It's like I'm only pretending to care when I do them. I just don't get any enjoyment out of it lately.
How long have you been feeling this loss of enjoyment in your usual activities?
I'd say this low, empty part has lasted about four months now. It started... well, long after this first big rush of energy I had at work passed. Ever since then, it's just been this flat feeling.
During that first rush of energy, did you feel unusually elevated or irritable compared with your normal mood?

Yeah, I did. At first, I felt almost unstoppable, you know? Like, extra cheerful and just completely on top of everything. But then it would flip, and I'd get really irritable. I'd snap hard over just small things. Like, if someone at work asked me to count my drawer again, I would just lose it on them. It was definitely not my normal way of acting.
How long did that unusually cheerful or irritable period last?
I'm not exactly sure how long it lasted, to be honest. It's hard to remember exactly when it started and stopped. I just know it was a while ago, before this whole flat feeling started.
At its longest, did that unusually cheerful or irritable period last at least four days in a row?

I'm honestly not sure if it was four days in a row. Like I said, it's hard to remember the exact timeline of it all. I wasn't really keeping track of the days... I just know it went on for a bit before all this flat feeling took over.
During that unusually cheerful or irritable period, did you need less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

Yeah, I did. With the changing shifts I have, I got to a point where I’d sleep only a few hours... but I'd still feel completely wired. And honestly, even now when I’m just exhausted, I wake up early and my mind is already going.
During that unusually energized period, were you talking more than usual or speaking noticeably faster?

Yeah, I definitely was. People at work actually kept telling me to slow down. I guess I was talking so fast about the schedules, the inventory, and all these ideas I had for the supervisors... I could just see it in their faces that they weren't following me at all. But I just had a lot to say right then, I guess.
During that unusually energized period, did you take on noticeably more projects or become much more productive and goal-directed than usual?

Yeah, definitely. I actually volunteered for extra cash-office work at the store, and I started reorganizing all the shelves on my own. I even... well, I planned out this whole promotion binder. I just had so much energy for all of it. And then I'd go home and still be going. I'd want to buy stuff online and completely rearrange my apartment instead of just sitting down to relax.
What is the longest number of consecutive days you felt unusually energized or irritable like that?
Honestly, I'm not really sure. I didn't exactly count the days while it was happening. It just... it felt like it went on for a while, but I couldn't give you a specific number.
Since this low, flat period began, has your appetite changed noticeably?

Yeah, it really has. It's been kind of all over the place, but lately... I mostly just forget to eat. Or if I do try to eat something, it just tastes like cardboard, so I don't finish it. I know I've lost some weight, too, because my work pants have been fitting a lot looser on me.
Have you had any thoughts about dying or killing yourself?

Yeah, I have. It's... I've had some pretty scary thoughts lately. Like, sometimes I just think maybe everyone would be better off if I didn't wake up. And a few times on the way home from work, I've actually caught myself looking at the cars and thinking about just stepping off the curb right into traffic.
Do you feel you might act on these thoughts today or soon?

No, I don't think so. I mean, they're just thoughts. I don't actually want to do it, it just... pops into my head sometimes when things feel really heavy. But I wouldn't actually do it today or anything like that.
Can you think of any specific events that help you estimate whether that unusually energized or irritable period lasted at least four days continuously?

Um, not really. I can't really think of a specific event or anything that would help track it. When I get like that, the days kind of just blur together, so... I'm not exactly sure how many days it was continuously.
Do you currently have a specific plan for how you would kill yourself?

No, I don't have a plan. It's really just... like I said, those thoughts about the traffic that just kind of happen. But I haven't sat down and figured out a way to actually do it or anything like that. So, no.
Was there ever a continuous stretch of at least four days when you felt unusually energized or irritable nearly every day?

Like I mentioned, it's hard to track the exact number of days, but yeah, there was definitely a stretch where I felt like that every day. For a while, I felt almost unstoppable... just extra cheerful and full of energy. But then I’d snap really hard over small things. Like at work, if someone asked me to count my register drawer again, I would just get so mad. So it was definitely a mix of being super energized and really irritable for a solid stretch of time.
